newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Phillips says US labor mart may be flexible.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Phillips says US labor mart may be flexible.

text.p: Federal Reserve Governor Susan Phillips said the U.S. labor market may be better able to cope with wage pressures than the low unemployment rate appears to suggest.
Speaking to reporters at Vanderbilt University here, Phillips said, "There may be more flexibility in the labor force than is implied by a low unemployment rate."
In addition, Phillips said that employers are finding ways to offset wage cost by holding down benefit outlays or improving productivity.
Asked about U.S. interest rates which have climbed recently, Phillips said, "The overall structure of interest rates is still relatively low."
Phillips declined to comment on whether rates were stimulative.
Turning to monetary policy, Phillips said the U.S. stock market was part of the economic scenario considered by the Fed during decision making.
"As a general matter, we do look at a variety of things and certainly the stock market is very important," Phillips said.
